newsitem.title: USA: Walden's Drever deal accretive in first year.
newsitem.headline: Walden's Drever deal accretive in first year.

text.p: Walden Residential Properties Inc said Wednesday its merger deal with privately-held Drever Partners Inc and affiliates is expected to be accretive to its funds from operations by about $0.10 a share in the first year of operations as a combined company.
Walden made the forecast as it announced the execution of a definitive agreement for the merger, which it initially disclosed on May 9.

Under the terms of the agreement, Drever and all of its apartment communities are expected to be acquired by Walden through a partnership unit in a transaction valued at approximately $670 million, it said. The combined company will continue to operate under the Walden corporate name.

The merger is subject to approval by regulators, Drever's investors and Walden's stockholders, will unite Drever's 18,118 multifamily units, located in Texas, Arizona, Georgia and California, with Walden's 22,878 units located in the Southeast and Southwest.
The deal, which is expected to be consummated by October 1997, will make Walden one of the nation's largest publicly traded apartment real estate investment trusts with approximately 41,000 units.
Total market capitalization is expected to exceed $1.5 billion upon completion of the transaction. For accounting purposes, the transaction will be treated as a purchase.
